newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power prices ease for Monday.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power prices ease for Monday.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly lower for Monday business in anticipation of an ease in frigid temperatures, power brokers and marketers said.

Temperatures were expected to be at least eight to 10 degrees below normal through the early weekend in much of the region, but were forecast to moderate through Sunday and return to near normal levels early next week.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Monday peak, non-firm power prices were discussed at $18.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from Thursday discussion at $32.00-43.00 for Friday delivery.
Off-peak Monday non-firm MAPP power eased to $12.00-14.00 from $16.00-19.00 on Thursday.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday were talked at $18.00-20.00 from $35.00-50.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak next day power was also said to be talked at $12.00-14.00 from $17.00-19.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday moved lower to $18.00-19.00 in the north and $24.00-26.00 in the south from a region-wide range of $40-46.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed lower at $13.00-15.00 for Monday from $15.00-18.00 per MWh on Thursday.
February ECAR was said to have held steady at $23.50-24.00.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery were talked at $20.00-22.00 through the entire region from $44.00-50.00 in the south and $36.00-40.00 in the north on Thursday.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were pegged at $13.00-15.00 from $17.00-20.00 on Thursday.
February SPP was said to have held steady at $23.00-24.00 per MWh, the sources said.
